newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Edison nuke seen up in several days.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Edison nuke seen up in several days.

text.p: Detroit Edison, operator of the 1,116 megawatt Fermi 2 nuclear power plant, said Thursday it will still be several days before the unit resumes electricity output.
"We expect turbine adjustments to take several days," spokeswoman Mary Kay Bean said, adding "The reactor is continuing to operate but the plant is not making power."
Detroit Edison interrupted restart of the plant on Monday after problems developed with a new turbine.
New equipment was installed during a maintenance and refueling outage which began September 27, 1996.
Detroit Edison owns and operates the Fermi plant, located in Monroe County, Mich.
The company is a subsidiary of DTE Energy Corp.
